newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Baht fall positive for Thai credit standing - S&P.
newsitem.headline: Baht fall positive for Thai credit standing - S&P.

text.p: The floating of the Thai baht should prove positive for Thailand's sovereign credit standing over time, a top official with Standard & Poor's Corp said.

"We see the depreciation in the Thai baht as a modest positive, something which should support the government's credit standing," David Beers, head of S&P's sovereign rating division told Reuters Financial Television (RFTV) in Sydney.
Beers said the government should earn a small dividend from the baht's fall as its dollar assets exceeded its liabilities.
It also would gain from higher revenue resulting from a pick-up in the economy as interest rates came down, he said.
However, Beers said the currency's decline would have negative consequences for those corporates highly leveraged in U.S. dollars and other foreign currencies.
The baht fell to record lows last week after the Thai government floated the currency in a bid to ease the worst economic slump in a decade.
S&P affirmed Thailand's long-term foreign currency debt at Single-A and its long-term local currency debt at AA last April.
